terminal.description: A shell in your workspace. Run your file here to see the cards it makes and changes.

tasks.title: Make a card
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 1` in `src/objects.js`, make `makeCandle(name, grams, priceCents)` return a new card: an object with the properties `name`, `grams` and `priceCents`, set from its parameters, and `stock`, set to `0`.

`makeCandle('Cedar', 200, 1800)` gives `{ name: 'Cedar', grams: 200, priceCents: 1800, stock: 0 }`.

Check calls `makeCandle` with candles of its own and compares every property of the card it gives back.
nextSteps: Read the lesson's part on making an object.
Return an object in curly braces from `makeCandle`.
Give it the four properties, each a name, a colon and a value, with commas between them.
Run the file: the first line should show the Cedar card.
hints: An object is written in curly braces, with a name and a value for each property.
The value of a property can be a parameter. `name: name` takes the value from the parameter called `name`; when the two names are the same you may write just `name`.
The function is one line: `return { name: name, grams: grams, ... }`, with `priceCents` and `stock: 0` in place of the dots.

tasks.title: Read any line of a card
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 2`, first write a function of your own called `hasLine`, from the word `function` to its closing brace. It has two parameters, `card` and `field`, and returns `true` when `card` has a property whose name is the text in `field`, and `false` when it does not. It only helps `cardLine`, so it stays off the `export` line.

Then make `cardLine(card, field)` return the name in `field`, a colon, a space and the value of that property: `'grams: 350'`. When the card has no property by that name, it returns `'scent: not on the card'`, with the name in `field` at the start. It calls `hasLine` to find out.

Check calls `hasLine` and `cardLine` with a card of its own, a property whose value is `0` included, and reads your file for `hasLine` and the call to it.
nextSteps: Read the lesson's parts on brackets and on asking whether a property is there.
Above `cardLine`, write `function hasLine(card, field) {` and its closing `}` yourself.
In `cardLine`, ask `hasLine` first, then read the property whose name is in `field`.
Run the file: the two lines for Task 2 should show grams and a missing scent.
hints: `field` holds the name of a property as text. A dot only works with a name written in the code itself.
Brackets with no quotes read the property whose name is inside a variable. Asking whether a property is there is a question of its own, with `in`: a value of `0` is there, though it counts as false.
`hasLine` is one line, `return field in card`, and `cardLine` starts ``if (hasLine(card, field)) { return `${field}: ${card[field]}` }``.

tasks.title: Sell from a card
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 3`, make `sell(card, count)` take `count` off the card's `stock`, changing the card itself, and return the card. When the stock reaches `0`, it also gives the card a property `soldOut` with the value `true`.

Check sells from cards of its own, never more than a card has in stock, and looks at the card it gave `sell` afterwards.
nextSteps: Read the lesson's part on changing and adding properties.
Give `card.stock` a new value: the old one minus `count`.
When the stock is now `0`, give the card `soldOut`.
Return the card and run the file.
hints: A property can be given a new value with a single `=`, the way a `let` can.
Giving a value to a property the object does not have yet adds that property. Ask about the stock after you have changed it, and compare with `===`.
The body has the shape `card.stock = card.stock - count`, then `if (card.stock === 0) { card.soldOut = true }`, then `return card`.

tasks.title: Restock a card
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 4`, make `restock(card, count)` add `count` to the card's `stock`, changing the card itself, remove the `soldOut` property when the card has one, and return the card.

Check restocks cards of its own, some sold out and some not, and looks at the card it gave `restock` afterwards. A removed property must be gone, not just hold a different value.
nextSteps: Read the lesson's part on removing a property.
Return the card and run the file: the Sage card should have stock and no soldOut.
hints: Giving `soldOut` the value `false` or `undefined` keeps the property on the card. The task asks for it to be gone.
`delete` removes a property from an object. Removing a property the object does not have does no harm, so there is no need to ask first.
The body has the shape `card.stock = card.stock + count`, then `delete card.soldOut`, then `return card`.
